en.title: Ghost Lights of the Rainforest

blocks.text: September 2019 ｜Bioluminescent Fungi Recorded at OneK Nature Reserve
In September 2019, during a nighttime survey at OneK Nature Reserve, we discovered a colony of bioluminescent fungi growing on a decaying log deep within the rainforest.

When our flashlights were turned off, the darkness of the forest suddenly revealed a soft green glow. Dozens of tiny mushrooms illuminated the rotting wood, appearing like miniature lanterns suspended in the night. Against the black backdrop of the rainforest, the scene felt almost otherworldly.

This phenomenon is known as bioluminescence—the production of light by living organisms. While fireflies and glowing click beetles are among the best-known bioluminescent creatures, certain fungi also possess the remarkable ability to emit light. More than one hundred species of luminous fungi have been documented worldwide, with tropical forests representing some of their most important habitats.

These fungi typically grow on decaying wood, where they play a critical ecological role as decomposers. By breaking down dead plant material, they help recycle nutrients back into the ecosystem, supporting the continuous renewal of the rainforest.

The green glow is produced through a biochemical reaction involving specialized compounds within the fungal tissues. Unlike artificial light sources, this process generates almost no heat and is therefore considered a form of cold light.

The ecological purpose of fungal bioluminescence remains an active area of scientific research. One leading hypothesis suggests that the glow attracts nocturnal insects, which may help disperse fungal spores as they move through the forest. In this way, the light may function as a biological advertisement, increasing the chances of successful reproduction and colonization of new habitats.

For many people, the rainforest at night is simply a place of darkness. Yet for those who venture into the forest after sunset, an entirely different world emerges. Hidden among fallen branches and decaying logs are organisms that transform darkness into light, revealing another dimension of tropical biodiversity.

This observation highlights the extraordinary diversity that exists within even the smallest rainforest microhabitats. A single fallen log, seemingly insignificant at first glance, can support a thriving community of organisms and produce one of nature’s most captivating displays.

Observation Date: September 2019
Location: OneK Nature Reserve, Costa Rica
Species: Bioluminescent Fungi
Behavior: Natural bioluminescence on decaying wood
Category: Fungal Ecology / Bioluminescence / Rainforest Night Observations

en.title: Why It Matters

blocks.text: Fungi are among the most important yet least studied organisms in tropical ecosystems. They drive nutrient cycling, support forest regeneration, and form essential links within ecological networks. By documenting unusual species and natural phenomena such as bioluminescent fungi, OneK contributes to a broader understanding of rainforest biodiversity beyond birds and mammals.
When darkness falls, the rainforest does not go to sleep. In some corners of the forest, life begins to glow. 🍄✨🌿

zh.title: 2019年9月 ｜OneK保护区记录生物发光蘑菇

blocks.text: 雨林里的绿色幽光
OneK保护区记录生物发光蘑菇
2019年9月，在OneK保护区的一次夜间调查中，我们在一段腐朽倒木上发现了一片会发光的蘑菇。
当手电关闭的瞬间，原本漆黑的森林里突然浮现出柔和的绿色光芒。数十个小小的菌盖散布在朽木表面，宛如一串漂浮在黑暗中的绿色灯笼，为雨林增添了一种神秘而梦幻的色彩。
这种现象被称为生物发光（Bioluminescence）。虽然萤火虫和发光叩甲较为人熟知，但事实上，部分真菌同样拥有发光能力。目前全球已知能够发光的真菌超过一百种，而热带雨林则是它们最重要的分布区域之一。
这些真菌通常生长在腐朽木材上，通过分解死亡植物组织参与森林中的养分循环。它们不仅是雨林分解者系统的重要成员，也承担着将枯死植物重新转化为生态系统可利用资源的重要角色。
真菌发光的原因至今仍是科学研究的热点课题。研究认为，这种绿色冷光来自真菌体内特殊化学物质与氧气发生反应所产生的生物发光现象。
关于发光的生态意义，目前存在多种假说。其中最广泛接受的观点认为，夜间发光能够吸引昆虫前来活动。当昆虫接触菌体后，真菌孢子可能附着于其身体表面，从而被携带到新的环境中扩散传播。

zh.title: 换句话说，这些发光蘑菇可能正在利用光芒吸引“运输工具”，帮助自己的后代传播到更远的森林角落。

blocks.text: 对于许多人来说，夜晚的雨林意味着黑暗。但对于真正走进森林的人而言，黑暗中同样充满生命。从会发光的昆虫，到会发光的真菌，雨林在夜晚展现出的生物多样性往往比白天更加令人惊叹。
这次记录不仅展示了热带雨林中罕见而美丽的自然现象，也提醒我们：即使是一截看似普通的朽木，也可能孕育着一个微小而神秘的生态世界。

观察时间： 2019年9月
观察地点： OneK自然保护区，哥斯达黎加
物种名称： 生物发光真菌（Bioluminescent Fungi）
记录内容： 生长于腐朽木材上的发光蘑菇群落
分类栏目： OneK Field Notes｜真菌生态与雨林夜间观察

zh.title: OneK意义

blocks.text: 真菌是热带雨林生态系统中最重要却最容易被忽视的生物类群之一。通过记录发光真菌等特殊物种，OneK不仅关注大型动物和鸟类，也关注维系森林运转的分解者系统。未来，OneK将持续开展夜间生物调查，探索雨林中更多隐藏于黑暗中的生命故事。
当夜色降临，森林并没有沉睡。相反，一些生命才刚刚开始发光。 🍄✨

en.title: November 26, 2019 | First Camera Trap Record of a Puma at OneK

blocks.text: On November 26, 2019, one of OneK’s camera traps captured the reserve’s first confirmed image of a Puma (Puma concolor).
This marked the first scientific record of the species within the reserve and became an important milestone in OneK’s long-term wildlife monitoring program.

In 2019, OneK established a camera trap network consisting of ten field-deployed cameras positioned throughout the reserve. Monitoring sites were selected along streams, ridgelines, wildlife trails, and other areas frequently used by mammals. Operating continuously day and night, the cameras were designed to document wildlife presence and activity patterns with minimal disturbance.
After months of monitoring, one camera successfully recorded a puma moving through the forest at night.

The puma is one of the largest wild cats in the Americas and has one of the widest distributions of any terrestrial mammal in the Western Hemisphere. Despite its broad range, the species is rarely observed directly due to its large home range, low population density, and highly elusive behavior.

en.title: Ecologically, pumas serve as apex predators.

blocks.text: By regulating populations of prey species, they help maintain ecological balance and contribute to the stability of forest ecosystems. The presence of apex predators is often considered a strong indicator of ecosystem integrity, habitat quality, and the existence of a functioning food web.
For this reason, the significance of this record extends far beyond documenting a single animal.
It provided evidence that the forest protected by OneK is capable of supporting large carnivores and continues to function as an important component of the regional ecological landscape.

Since then, OneK’s camera trap program has continued to document pumas, ocelots, and many other mammal species, generating valuable data that supports conservation planning and long-term ecological monitoring.

en.title: Looking back, the image recorded on November 26, 2019 was more than a wildlife photograph.

blocks.text: It was a confirmation that the forest was still alive, connected, and capable of sustaining one of the Americas’ most iconic predators.

zh.title: 2019年11月26日｜红外相机首次记录到美洲狮

blocks.text: 2019年11月26日，OneK野外布设的10台红外相机首次记录到美洲狮（Puma concolor）的活动影像。
这是 OneK 保护区历史上首次通过科学监测设备确认美洲狮的存在，也是保护区长期野生动物监测工作的重要里程碑之一。
为了了解保护区内大型哺乳动物的分布情况，我们自2019年开始在森林中布设红外相机监测网络。监测点覆盖溪流、山脊、森林通道以及野生动物经常活动的区域，通过全天候自动拍摄的方式记录野生动物的活动情况。

zh.title: 经过持续监测后，其中一台红外相机成功拍摄到美洲狮夜间经过森林的画面。

blocks.text: 作为美洲最大的猫科动物之一，美洲狮广泛分布于美洲大陆。然而，由于其活动范围广、密度较低且行为隐秘，即使在拥有稳定种群的区域，人们也很少能够直接观察到它们。
对于生态系统而言，美洲狮属于顶级捕食者。
它们通过捕食中大型食草动物和其他猎物，维持生态系统内部的种群平衡，对森林生态健康具有重要作用。顶级捕食者的存在，往往意味着生态系统拥有相对完整的食物链结构和足够的栖息地资源。

zh.title: 因此，这次记录不仅仅代表发现了一只美洲狮。

blocks.text: 更重要的是，它证明了 OneK 所保护的森林能够支持大型捕食者的生存，并在区域生态网络中发挥着重要作用。
从那以后，红外相机持续记录到包括美洲狮、虎猫以及其他野生哺乳动物在内的大量珍贵影像资料，为保护区的长期监测工作提供了重要科学依据。
回顾今天，2019年11月26日记录到的那段影像，不仅是一份珍贵的数据。
它更像是一种来自森林的回应。
告诉我们，这片土地正在发挥它应有的生态价值。

en.title: January 2020 ｜Hundreds of Urania fulgens Attracted to Dog Feces for Mineral Feeding

blocks.text: In January 2020, OneK Nature Reserve documented an unusual and fascinating insect aggregation. Hundreds of Moon Moths (Urania fulgens) were observed congregating around a pile of dog feces along a forest trail, creating an impressive spectacle rarely witnessed in the rainforest.

At first glance, the scene appeared unusual. Rather than visiting flowers for nectar, the moths were concentrated on the ground, actively probing the feces with their proboscises. Continuous observation revealed that the insects were feeding on dissolved minerals and nutrients contained within the organic material.

Although Urania fulgens is commonly admired for its striking metallic green and black wings and butterfly-like appearance, it is actually a member of the moth family Uraniidae. Like many butterflies and moths, adult individuals require more than just sugar-rich nectar. Essential minerals such as sodium, nitrogen compounds, and amino acids are often scarce in floral resources and must be obtained from alternative sources.

This behavior, commonly known as mineral feeding or mud-puddling, occurs when insects gather on nutrient-rich substrates such as mud, animal feces, carrion, decaying fruit, or even sweat. These resources provide critical nutrients that support metabolism, reproduction, and overall fitness.

For many Lepidoptera, especially males, the minerals collected during feeding can later be transferred to females during mating through nutrient-rich spermatophores. In this way, the nutrients obtained from these temporary feeding sites may contribute directly to reproductive success and offspring development.

The large number of individuals observed at a single fecal source suggests that such nutrient resources may represent valuable and sometimes limited opportunities within the rainforest environment. While flowers provide energy, these less conspicuous resources supply elements that are equally important for survival.

Urania fulgens is one of the most iconic day-flying moths of Central America and is also known for regional migratory movements. Observations such as this reveal a lesser-known aspect of its ecology and highlight the complex nutritional strategies employed by rainforest insects.

This record serves as a reminder that even the most ordinary features of the forest floor can play an important ecological role. A small pile of animal feces became a temporary feeding station for hundreds of insects, demonstrating how nutrients move through tropical ecosystems in unexpected ways.

Observation Date: January 2020
Location: OneK Nature Reserve, Costa Rica
Species: Urania fulgens
Behavior: Mass aggregation on dog feces for mineral and nutrient acquisition
Category: Insect Behavior / Nutrient Ecology / Rainforest Natural History Observations

en.title: Why It Matters

blocks.text: This observation documents an important but often overlooked aspect of insect ecology. By recording mineral-feeding events and aggregation behavior, OneK contributes valuable natural history data that helps improve our understanding of nutrient cycling, insect nutrition, and the ecological dynamics of tropical rainforest communities.

zh.title: 2020年1月｜数百只 Urania fulgens 被狗粪吸引聚集取食矿物质

blocks.text: 2020年1月，OneK保护区记录到一次特殊的昆虫聚集现象。数百只月亮蛾（Urania fulgens）聚集在林道旁的一处区域，而吸引它们的并非花朵或果实，而是一堆狗的粪便。
在观察过程中，大量个体持续停留在粪便表面，通过口器吸取其中的液体和溶解矿物质。聚集数量达到数百只，形成了十分壮观的场景。
对于许多鳞翅目昆虫而言，花蜜主要提供能量来源，但往往缺乏钠、氨基酸及其他重要矿物元素。因此，它们经常会从动物粪便、腐烂果实、尸体、泥地甚至汗液中补充这些资源。这种行为被称为矿物质摄取（Mineral Feeding）或吸盐行为（Mud-puddling）。
月亮蛾虽然属于蛾类，但和许多蝴蝶一样，也会利用这些特殊资源补充营养。动物粪便中富含氮化合物、氨基酸以及多种微量元素，对于成虫维持代谢活动和繁殖能力具有重要意义。
尤其是雄性个体，获取到的矿物质和氮源还可能在交配过程中通过精包（spermatophore）转移给雌虫，从而提高后代的生存机会。因此，这类看似“不太优雅”的行为，实际上是昆虫繁殖策略的重要组成部分。
Urania fulgens 是中美洲最著名的昼行性蛾类之一，以其金属绿色闪耀的翅膀而闻名。该物种同时也是重要的迁飞昆虫，在中美洲和加勒比地区会进行区域性迁移。
此次记录不仅展示了月亮蛾鲜为人知的一面，也提醒我们：在雨林生态系统中，看似普通甚至令人忽略的资源，往往对野生动物具有重要价值。

观察时间： 2020年1月
观察地点： OneK自然保护区，哥斯达黎加
物种名称： 月亮蛾（Urania fulgens）
记录内容： 数百只个体聚集于狗粪表面摄取矿物质与盐分
分类栏目： OneK Field Notes｜昆虫行为与自然历史观察

zh.title: OneK意义

blocks.text: 这次观察记录了热带昆虫获取矿物质资源的一种典型行为。与花蜜取食相比，矿物质摄取往往持续时间短、机会性强，因此较少被记录。通过长期监测类似现象，OneK希望进一步了解昆虫营养需求、迁飞行为以及其在雨林生态系统中的生态角色，为区域生物多样性研究积累更多基础资料。

en.title: April 2020 | Seven Puma Records in Just Fifteen Days

blocks.text: In April 2020, OneK’s camera trap monitoring program achieved a remarkable milestone.
Within a period of just fifteen days, camera traps deployed throughout the reserve recorded seven separate detections of a Puma (Puma concolor).
Less than six months had passed since OneK’s first confirmed camera trap record of a puma in November 2019, making these repeated detections both surprising and encouraging.

Pumas are among the most elusive predators in the Americas. With large home ranges, primarily nocturnal behavior, and exceptional stealth, they are rarely observed directly, even in areas where stable populations exist.
Yet during April 2020, camera traps documented puma activity on seven separate occasions across the reserve.

These repeated records suggested that OneK was more than just a corridor occasionally used by a wandering individual. Instead, the reserve appeared to form part of a regularly utilized landscape within the species’ local range.
As apex predators, pumas occupy the highest level of the food web. Their presence reflects the availability of prey, the quality of habitat, and the overall ecological integrity of an ecosystem.

For a young private reserve, repeated records of a top predator represented a strong indication that conservation efforts were helping maintain a functioning and biologically rich rainforest environment.
The observations also reinforced the value of long-term camera trap monitoring as a tool for understanding wildlife activity and evaluating conservation outcomes.

en.title: Looking back, seven puma records in fifteen days were more than a monitoring result.

blocks.text: They were evidence that the forest remained connected, healthy, and capable of supporting one of the Americas’ most iconic predators.
For us, it was a powerful reminder that protecting habitat truly makes a difference.

zh.title: 2020年4月｜15天内7次记录美洲狮活动

blocks.text: 2020年4月，OneK红外相机监测项目取得了一项令人振奋的成果。
在短短15天时间内，布设于保护区内的红外相机共记录到7次美洲狮（Puma concolor）活动影像。
距离2019年11月首次拍摄到美洲狮仅过去不到半年时间，这一结果远远超出了我们的预期。
对于大型猫科动物而言，直接观察本就极为困难。美洲狮拥有广阔的活动范围，主要在夜间活动，并且具有极强的隐蔽性。因此，即使在存在稳定种群的区域，人们也很少能够频繁记录到它们的活动。

zh.title: 然而，在2020年4月的监测数据中，美洲狮却连续多次出现在不同监测点位。

blocks.text: 这一结果表明，OneK保护区不仅仅是美洲狮偶尔经过的森林，而很可能已经成为其长期活动范围的重要组成部分。
作为新热带雨林中的顶级捕食者，美洲狮位于食物链顶端。它们的存在意味着森林中拥有足够的猎物资源、完整的栖息地结构以及相对健康的生态系统。
对于一个成立不久的私人保护区而言，能够持续记录到顶级捕食者活动，是生态保护成效的重要体现。
这些影像记录不仅让我们更加了解保护区内大型哺乳动物的活动规律，也坚定了我们继续开展长期监测和生态保护工作的信心。
回顾今天，15天内7次记录美洲狮并不仅仅是一组数据。
它更像是森林给予我们的答案。
证明这片土地正在为野生动物提供一个安全的家园。

en.title: October 2021 ｜A Remarkable Breeding Record from OneK Nature Reserve

blocks.text: In October 2021, a breeding pair of Grey-tailed Trogons (Trogon massena) was observed nesting inside a large arboreal termite nest within OneK Nature Reserve, Costa Rica.

The discovery was made during routine biodiversity monitoring when an adult trogon was seen repeatedly entering and leaving a cavity excavated in the side of an active termite structure suspended between the branches of a rainforest tree. Continued observations confirmed that the cavity was being used as a nesting chamber, providing a rare opportunity to document this remarkable breeding strategy within the reserve.

Unlike woodpeckers, trogons lack the strong chisel-like bills required to excavate solid wood. Instead, several Neotropical trogon species have evolved a unique nesting behavior: they carve nesting cavities into soft substrates such as decaying wood, rotten stumps, wasp nests, and particularly arboreal termite nests. The compact yet relatively soft outer walls of termite nests can be excavated with considerably less effort than living wood, while still providing excellent protection for eggs and nestlings.

Termite nests offer several advantages as nesting sites. Their thick walls help buffer temperature fluctuations, maintain stable humidity, and conceal nests from predators. Elevated above the forest floor, they also reduce the risk of flooding and provide additional protection from many terrestrial predators. These characteristics create a favorable microclimate for successful breeding in the humid tropical rainforest.

The relationship between trogons and termites is generally considered a form of commensalism. The birds benefit from the nest structure as a secure breeding site, while the termite colony is usually only minimally affected. In many cases, termites continue to occupy and maintain portions of the nest even while the birds are nesting nearby.

This observation highlights one of the many intricate ecological relationships found within tropical rainforests. A structure built by thousands of termites ultimately becomes a breeding chamber for one of the forest’s most charismatic birds, illustrating how different species can become interconnected through the resources they create and utilize.

The Grey-tailed Trogon is one of the characteristic birds of the lowland rainforests of Central America. Although frequently heard calling from the forest canopy and edges, opportunities to observe its nesting behavior are uncommon. This breeding record therefore represents an important natural history observation for OneK Nature Reserve and contributes to our growing understanding of cavity-nesting birds and rainforest ecosystem interactions.

Observation Date: October 2021
Location: OneK Nature Reserve, Costa Rica
Species: Grey-tailed Trogon (Trogon massena)
Behavior: Nesting and breeding within an arboreal termite nest
Category: Breeding Biology / Cavity Nesting Ecology / Rainforest Natural History Observations
“In the rainforest, even a termite nest can become the nursery of a trogon—an elegant reminder that one species’ architecture may become another species’ home.”

zh.title: 2021年10月 OneK保护区记录灰尾美洲咬鹃利用树栖白蚁巢繁殖

blocks.text: 2021年10月｜OneK保护区记录灰尾美洲咬鹃利用树栖白蚁巢繁殖
2021年10月，OneK保护区在日常生物多样性监测过程中，记录到一对灰尾美洲咬鹃（Trogon massena）在树栖白蚁巢内筑巢繁殖。
最初，我们发现成鸟频繁进出一个悬挂于树干之间的大型白蚁巢。经过持续观察，确认其在白蚁巢侧面开凿出巢洞，并将其作为繁殖巢穴使用。这是OneK保护区首次完整记录到灰尾美洲咬鹃利用树栖白蚁巢进行繁殖的行为。
与啄木鸟不同，咬鹃并不具备强壮的凿木能力，无法在坚硬的树干中开凿巢洞。因此，在长期演化过程中，许多新热带地区的咬鹃发展出一种独特的繁殖策略——利用腐木、朽木树桩、蜂巢以及树栖白蚁巢等较软的结构作为筑巢场所。
树栖白蚁巢虽然外表坚固，但其内部结构相对松软，咬鹃能够利用喙部轻松开凿出适合育雏的巢室。同时，白蚁巢厚实的外壁还能够提供良好的隔热和保温效果，帮助维持稳定的温度与湿度，为鸟蛋和雏鸟创造适宜的发育环境。
从生态学角度来看，这是一种典型的资源利用关系。白蚁通过长期建设形成庞大的巢体，而咬鹃则利用这一现成结构完成繁殖。一个由数百万只白蚁共同建造的“建筑工程”，最终成为了雨林鸟类的育婴室。
灰尾美洲咬鹃是中美洲低地雨林最具代表性的鸟类之一。虽然它们的叫声经常回荡在森林之中，但真正观察到其筑巢和繁殖行为的机会并不多。因此，这次记录不仅丰富了OneK保护区的繁殖鸟类资料，也为了解雨林洞穴生态系统（Cavity Ecosystem）提供了宝贵的自然历史观察记录。
这项发现再次提醒我们，雨林中的生态关系远比表面所见更加复杂。一个白蚁巢不仅是白蚁的家园，也可能成为鸟类、昆虫、爬行动物甚至微生物共同利用的重要生态资源。

观察地点： OneK自然保护区，哥斯达黎加

en.title: March 2022 ｜A Rare White Hummingbird Recorded at OneK Nature Reserve

blocks.text: An Unexpected Discovery in the Rainforest
In March 2022, during a routine biodiversity survey at OneK Nature Reserve, our team recorded one of the most unusual birds ever observed within the reserve: a rare white hummingbird.

Perched quietly among rainforest vines and understory vegetation, the bird immediately stood out from its surroundings. Unlike the vibrant greens, blues, and iridescent colors commonly associated with tropical hummingbirds, this individual displayed almost entirely white plumage, creating a striking contrast against the deep green rainforest backdrop.

For field naturalists and bird observers, encounters with abnormal color morphs are exceptionally rare. The observation was documented through photographs and field notes and has since become one of the most remarkable records in OneK’s biodiversity archives.

en.title: Understanding Leucism

blocks.text: Although such birds are often described as “albino,” many white birds are actually affected by a different condition known as leucism.

Leucism is a genetic pigmentation anomaly that results in the partial or complete loss of feather coloration while leaving the eyes and other soft tissues largely unaffected. In contrast, true albinism involves the complete absence of melanin throughout the body and is typically associated with pink or red eyes.
Based on the photographs and field observations, the OneK individual is believed to represent a leucistic hummingbird rather than a true albino bird.
Color abnormalities of this kind have been documented in many bird families worldwide, but they remain uncommon, particularly among hummingbirds.

en.title: Surviving as a White Hummingbird

blocks.text: For a hummingbird, unusual coloration may come with significant challenges.

Hummingbirds rely on speed, agility, and often subtle coloration to avoid predators and interact with other members of their species. An individual with bright white plumage may be more visible to predators and may experience differences in social or breeding interactions.
The fact that this bird survived long enough to be observed in the wild highlights both the resilience of the individual and the ecological integrity of the habitat that supports it.

en.title: Why Long-Term Monitoring Matters

blocks.text: Rare observations like this are one of the reasons long-term biodiversity monitoring is so important.

Many of nature’s most fascinating events occur unexpectedly and may never be documented without consistent field presence. At OneK, daily observations, wildlife surveys, camera-trap monitoring, and species inventories allow us to record not only common wildlife but also unusual and scientifically valuable occurrences.
Each observation contributes to a deeper understanding of tropical rainforest ecosystems and helps build a long-term record of biodiversity within the reserve.

en.title: A Reminder of Nature’s Endless Surprises

blocks.text: The discovery of this white hummingbird serves as a reminder that even after years of exploration, tropical rainforests continue to reveal unexpected wonders.
From rare behaviors and unique ecological interactions to extraordinary individual animals, every observation adds another piece to the story of biodiversity.

At OneK Nature Reserve, we remain committed to documenting, protecting, and sharing these stories, ensuring that the remarkable diversity of Costa Rica’s rainforests continues to inspire future generations.

zh.title: 2022年3月 ｜OneK记录到罕见白化蜂鸟

blocks.text: 雨林中的白色精灵
2022年3月，在 OneK Nature Reserve 的一次日常生物多样性调查中，我们记录到了一只极为罕见的白色蜂鸟个体。
当时，这只蜂鸟静静停栖在雨林林下的藤本植物之间。与热带雨林中常见的绿色、蓝色或金属光泽羽色的蜂鸟不同，它几乎全身呈现纯白色，在翠绿的森林背景映衬下显得格外醒目，仿佛一位来自雨林深处的白色精灵。
对于长期从事野外观察的人来说，这样的发现十分难得。即使在生物多样性极其丰富的热带雨林中，拥有异常羽色的蜂鸟也极少被记录到。

zh.title: 什么是“白化”现象？

blocks.text: 许多人会将这样的个体称为“白化动物”，但从科学角度来看，它更有可能属于一种被称为“白变”（Leucism）的色素异常现象。
白变是一种遗传性的羽毛色素缺失现象，会导致鸟类部分或全部羽毛失去正常颜色，从而呈现白色或浅色外观。而真正的白化症（Albinism）则是完全无法产生黑色素，通常伴随着红色或粉红色眼睛等特征。
根据当时的观察记录和影像资料判断，这只蜂鸟很可能属于白变个体，而非真正意义上的白化个体。
虽然类似现象在世界各地的鸟类中偶有记录，但在蜂鸟身上依然十分罕见，因此具有重要的自然历史记录价值。

zh.title: 在自然界中生存并不容易

blocks.text: 对于蜂鸟而言，异常的羽色并不一定是一种优势。
蜂鸟不仅需要依靠敏捷的飞行能力躲避天敌，还需要通过羽色和行为完成种内识别、求偶和领地活动。纯白色羽毛可能使其更容易被捕食者发现，也可能影响与同类之间的互动。
正因如此，能够在野外成长并被观察到的白变个体并不多见。
这只蜂鸟能够在雨林中自由活动，本身就是一个令人惊叹的生命故事。

zh.title: 长期监测带来的珍贵发现

blocks.text: OneK 长期坚持开展生物多样性调查与生态监测工作，持续记录保护区内的鸟类、昆虫、两栖爬行动物、哺乳动物以及植物资源。
许多珍贵的发现并非来自一次专门的寻找，而是源于日复一日的持续观察。
正是因为长期驻守在这片雨林之中，我们才有机会记录到这样罕见而特殊的个体。
每一次观察、每一张照片、每一条记录，都是了解热带生态系统的重要线索，也共同构成了 OneK 生物多样性档案的一部分。
雨林永远充满惊喜
热带雨林是地球上生命最丰富的生态系统之一。

zh.title: 在这里，我们见证过罕见的动物行为、记录过新的物种分布，也发现过许多令人难以置信的自然现象。

blocks.text: 这只白色蜂鸟的出现，再一次提醒我们：
大自然总会以意想不到的方式带来惊喜。
而保护这些生态系统，不仅是在保护已知的生命，也是在守护那些尚未被发现的奇迹。

en.title: May 2023 First Record of a Sunbittern at OneK Nature Reserve

blocks.text: | OneK Field Notes
In May 2023, we recorded our first observation of a Sunbittern (Eurypyga helias) along a forest stream within OneK Nature Reserve.

The bird was observed foraging quietly along the edge of a shaded creek, moving slowly among rocks, leaf litter, and shallow water. Its cryptic plumage blended remarkably well with the surrounding environment, making it nearly invisible against the forest floor.
Although the Sunbittern is widely distributed throughout tropical America, it is often difficult to observe due to its secretive behavior and preference for densely vegetated stream corridors.
For OneK, this observation was particularly exciting because the species is closely associated with well-preserved forest waterways and undisturbed riparian habitats.

en.title: A Specialist of Forest Streams

blocks.text: Unlike herons and many other wading birds that frequent open wetlands, the Sunbittern is primarily a bird of shaded rivers, streams, and forested watersheds.
It feeds on small aquatic animals, insects, crustaceans, and other invertebrates found along stream margins.
Its presence often reflects the availability of intact streamside habitat and healthy freshwater ecosystems.

en.title: More Than a Single Observation

blocks.text: What began as a single wildlife encounter would later become part of a much larger story.
Following this first record, additional observations confirmed that Sunbitterns regularly used waterways within the reserve.
Subsequent monitoring eventually led to the discovery of nesting activity, providing evidence that the species was not merely passing through the area but was utilizing the habitat for reproduction.

en.title: Why This Observation Matters

blocks.text: Many important conservation outcomes are first noticed through simple field observations.
The appearance of a Sunbittern does not prove ecological recovery on its own, but it does suggest that protected forest streams can continue to provide habitat for specialized wildlife.
For us, this first encounter marked the beginning of a deeper understanding of the reserve’s freshwater ecosystem and the species that depend upon it.

zh.title: 2023年5月｜OneK首次记录日鳽

blocks.text: 2023年5月｜OneK发现与记录（Discoveries & Observations）
2023年5月，我们在OneK保护区内的一条森林溪流旁，首次记录到日鳽（Eurypyga helias）的活动。
当时，这只日鳽出现在被雨林植被覆盖的溪流边缘，缓慢地沿着河岸觅食。它时而停留在溪边岩石上，时而在浅水区域行走，寻找昆虫、小型甲壳动物及其他无脊椎动物作为食物。
由于其羽毛颜色与枯叶、岩石和河岸环境极为相似，即使在近距离观察时，也很容易被忽略。正是这种出色的伪装能力，使日鳽成为热带雨林溪流生态系统中最神秘的鸟类之一。

zh.title: 森林溪流中的隐居者

blocks.text: 日鳽广泛分布于中南美洲热带地区，但与许多涉水鸟类不同，它并不喜欢开阔湿地或大型河流。
相反，它更偏好保存完好的森林溪流、阴湿河谷以及植被茂密的河岸环境。
它们通常独自活动，警觉性极高，一旦受到惊扰便会迅速飞离。在飞行过程中，日鳽会展开翅膀，露出极具特色的橙色、黑色和白色斑纹，用来震慑潜在的捕食者。
然而在平时，大多数时间它们都隐藏在森林阴影之中，因此能够观察到日鳽本身就是一件并不容易的事情。

zh.title: 一次重要的观察记录

blocks.text: 对于OneK而言，这次记录不仅增加了保护区的鸟类名录，更让我们对保护区河流生态系统有了新的认识。
日鳽是一种高度依赖森林溪流环境的鸟类，它们需要稳定的水源、完整的河岸植被以及丰富的无脊椎动物资源。
因此，它们的出现往往意味着溪流生态系统仍然保持着较好的自然状态。
作为长期开展河流保护与生物多样性监测工作的保护区，我们非常高兴看到这样的物种出现在OneK的森林中。

zh.title: 从首次发现到长期观察

blocks.text: 最初，这只是一次偶然的相遇。
但在随后的几年里，我们又陆续多次记录到日鳽的活动。
这些持续的观察表明，日鳽并非偶然经过OneK，而是长期利用保护区内的溪流生境。
更令人振奋的是，后来我们还在保护区内发现了日鳽的巢址，并成功记录到其繁殖行为。
这意味着OneK不仅能够为日鳽提供觅食场所，也能够为其提供繁殖所需的安全栖息环境。

zh.title: 为什么这条记录值得被记住

blocks.text: 许多重要的生态发现，往往开始于一次简单的观察。
2023年5月的这只日鳽，也许只是溪流边一个短暂的身影。
但它让我们看见了森林深处正在发生的变化。
它提醒我们，当森林被持续保护，当河流保持自然状态时，那些依赖健康生态系统生存的物种终将回到这里。
而对于OneK来说，这也是我们记录雨林生命故事的开始。

en.title: May 2023 ｜The Bee-Mimicking Katydid: More Than Just a Look-Alike

blocks.text: In 2023, a remarkable katydid was documented within the OneK Nature Reserve: the Bee-Mimicking Katydid (Aganacris velutina).

At first glance, it hardly resembles a katydid at all. Instead, it appears strikingly similar to a stinging bee. Its black-and-orange coloration, slender body shape, and quick, erratic movements create a convincing illusion of a hymenopteran insect. What made this observation particularly fascinating was that the mimicry extended beyond appearance. The insect’s antennae moved in a manner remarkably similar to those of foraging bees, constantly probing and scanning its surroundings.

This is an excellent example of protective mimicry, an evolutionary strategy in which a harmless species gains protection by resembling a more dangerous or unpalatable one. Although Aganacris velutina cannot sting, predators may avoid it because it resembles insects capable of defending themselves.

In tropical rainforests, successful mimicry often involves more than color and shape. Natural selection can favor behavioral traits as well, including movement patterns, posture, and even the way an insect uses its antennae. By combining visual and behavioral deception, species such as Aganacris velutina increase their chances of avoiding predation.

Observations like this highlight one of the rainforest’s most fascinating themes: evolution does not simply create organisms—it creates convincing illusions. Every field encounter offers another glimpse into the complex relationships between predators, prey, and the remarkable adaptations that have evolved over millions of years.

zh.title: 2023年5月｜拟蜂螽：不只是长得像蜂

blocks.text: 2023年5月｜OneK 保护区记录到一种极具迷惑性的螽斯——拟蜂螽 Aganacris velutina。
第一眼看去，它几乎不像一只螽斯，而更像一只具有警戒色的蜂。它黑橙相间的体色、细长的身体轮廓，以及快速而不规则的动作，都在模仿蜂类。更令人惊讶的是，它不仅“长得像”，连触角的抖动方式也极像蜂在搜索、探测环境时的动作。
这种现象属于典型的拟态防御。螽斯本身并不会像蜂一样蜇刺，但通过模拟蜂类的外形和行为，可以让捕食者误以为它具有危险性，从而减少被攻击的机会。研究中也记录到 Aganacris 属螽斯会模拟蜂类的快速移动、触角探测和身体姿态，是新热带雨林中非常精彩的拟蜂昆虫类群。
这次观察提醒我们，雨林中的拟态并不只是颜色和形状的相似，更包括动作、节奏和行为细节。OneK 的每一次野外记录，都是打开雨林演化故事的一扇小窗。

en.title: February 2024 | Life Within a Fallen Log: A Longhorn Beetle Breeding Aggregation

blocks.text: During a night survey in February 2024, we observed an unusual concentration of longhorn beetles (Family Cerambycidae) on a single decaying log within OneK Nature Reserve.

Over the course of one evening, five adult beetles were found on the same piece of dead wood. Several individuals were observed mating, while others appeared to be selecting oviposition sites and laying eggs within cracks and crevices of the decomposing timber.

Although longhorn beetles are common components of tropical forest ecosystems, witnessing multiple individuals simultaneously engaged in reproductive behavior on the same log offered a rare opportunity to observe an important stage of the rainforest life cycle.

en.title: Why Do They Gather on the Same Log?

blocks.text: For many longhorn beetle species, dead and decaying wood is far more than shelter—it is the nursery for the next generation.

Female beetles carefully select suitable wood in which to deposit their eggs. After hatching, the larvae tunnel deep into the timber, feeding on wood tissues and the fungi associated with the decomposition process.
Depending on the species, larval development may take months or even years before the beetles finally emerge as adults.
For these insects, finding the right log is one of the most important decisions in their life cycle.

en.title: A Fallen Tree Is Not Dead

blocks.text: In a tropical rainforest, a fallen tree is not the end of life—it is the beginning of a new ecological community.
Decaying logs provide habitat for a remarkable diversity of organisms, including:

items: Scarab beetles and other wood-associated insects;

blocks.text: Together, these organisms break down dead wood and recycle nutrients back into the forest ecosystem.
Longhorn beetles play an important role in this process, helping accelerate decomposition and contributing to nutrient cycling within the rainforest.

en.title: Engineers of the Forest Floor

blocks.text: The adult stage of many longhorn beetles is relatively short.
Their primary purpose is reproduction—finding mates and ensuring the next generation can develop successfully within suitable wood.
Once eggs are laid, the larvae begin the slow process of transforming dead timber into organic matter that eventually becomes part of the forest soil.
In this way, longhorn beetles are not simply insects; they are key participants in the rainforest’s recycling system.
Without decomposers such as beetles, fungi, and termites, nutrients would remain locked inside dead trees rather than being returned to the ecosystem.

en.title: Why This Observation Matters

blocks.text: While the beetles themselves may not be rare, observing multiple individuals gathering on a single log for mating and egg-laying is an important natural history record.
It offers a glimpse into a process that is usually hidden from view:
the transformation of death into new life.
For OneK, this observation highlights the ecological importance of dead wood habitats and reinforces the value of protecting natural decomposition processes within tropical forests.
Every fallen tree continues to support life long after it stops growing.

zh.title: 2024年2月｜朽木上的生命循环：长臂天牛的繁殖聚集

blocks.text: 2024年2月的一次夜间巡查中，我们在OneK保护区内的一段大型朽木上发现了一场特殊的聚集活动。
在不到一米长的木段上，共观察到5只大型长臂天牛（Longhorn Beetles），其中部分个体正在交配，而另一些个体则停留在木材表面进行产卵活动。
对于大多数人而言，这或许只是几只昆虫停留在一块腐木上。
但从生态学角度来看，这实际上是热带雨林中一个重要而完整的生命循环正在发生。

zh.title: 为什么它们会聚集在同一块朽木上？

blocks.text: 对于许多天牛来说，朽木不仅是栖息地，更是下一代生存的基础。
雌虫会寻找适合幼虫发育的木材，并将卵产在树皮裂缝、腐朽组织或木材内部。
幼虫孵化后会钻入木材之中，利用木质组织和其中的真菌群落作为食物来源，并在其中完成长达数月甚至数年的发育过程。
因此，对于这些天牛而言：
寻找合适的朽木，就等于为下一代寻找生长的摇篮。

zh.title: 一块朽木，也是一座生态系统

blocks.text: 在热带雨林中，倒木并非“死亡的树木”。
相反，它们往往是生物多样性最丰富的微生境之一。
一块腐朽木材中可能同时生活着：

zh.title: 这些生物共同参与木材分解过程，将原本坚硬的木质组织逐渐转化为土壤养分。

blocks.text: 而天牛正是这一过程中的重要成员之一。
从成虫到森林养分循环
成虫阶段的天牛寿命往往并不长。
它们羽化后的主要任务是寻找配偶并完成繁殖。
当雌虫将卵产入木材后，新一代幼虫便开始参与森林中的分解过程。
从某种意义上说，天牛不仅是昆虫。
它们也是森林养分循环系统中的“工程师”。
通过不断分解死亡树木，它们帮助森林完成物质循环，使养分重新回到土壤之中，为新的植物生长提供支持。

zh.title: 为什么这次观察值得记录？

blocks.text: 虽然天牛并不属于稀有物种，但能够同时观察到多只个体聚集、交配和产卵，却并不常见。
这样的场景让我们得以直接观察一个关键生态过程：
死亡的树木如何孕育新的生命。
对于OneK而言，这次记录不仅增加了保护区昆虫观察资料，也展示了热带雨林中常被忽略却至关重要的生态功能——朽木生态系统（Dead Wood Ecosystem）。
在雨林里，一棵树的生命结束，并不意味着故事的结束。
很多时候，它恰恰是另一个生命故事的开始。

blocks.text: July 2025 ｜Recording a Costa Rican Endemic Bird: Black-cheeked Ant-Tanager (Driophlox atrimaxillaris)
In July 2025, OneK Biological Station recorded one of Costa Rica’s most remarkable endemic birds—the Black-cheeked Ant-Tanager (Driophlox atrimaxillaris).

Found only in the humid lowland rainforests of southwestern Costa Rica, particularly around the Osa Peninsula and Golfo Dulce region, this species has one of the most restricted distributions of any bird in the country. Its presence is closely associated with well-preserved tropical rainforest, making it an important indicator of habitat quality.

The Black-cheeked Ant-Tanager inhabits the forest understory and dense shrub layer, where it forages for insects, small invertebrates, and fruits. Although its common name includes “Ant-Tanager,” it is not a true antbird. Nevertheless, it often occurs in the same dark, densely vegetated rainforest habitats favored by many ant-following species.

Unlike many colorful tropical birds, the Black-cheeked Ant-Tanager is often overlooked due to its secretive behavior. Most observations come from brief encounters or vocal detections deep within the forest. Obtaining clear photographic documentation of the species is therefore always a rewarding experience for field researchers and bird observers.

The species is considered vulnerable to habitat fragmentation and forest degradation. Studies have shown that it prefers mature, intact rainforest and is less common in disturbed habitats. As a result, its continued presence serves as a valuable indicator of healthy forest ecosystems.

For OneK Biological Station, this observation represents more than just another bird record. It highlights the importance of long-term rainforest conservation and habitat protection efforts. The occurrence of a regional endemic species such as the Black-cheeked Ant-Tanager demonstrates that the reserve continues to provide suitable habitat for some of Costa Rica’s most specialized wildlife.

As OneK expands its biodiversity monitoring programs, endemic species like the Black-cheeked Ant-Tanager will remain key focal points for understanding ecosystem health and measuring the long-term success of conservation efforts.

zh.title: 2025年7月｜记录到哥斯达黎加特有鸟——黑颊蚁唐纳雀

blocks.text: 2025年7月，OneK Biological Station 在保护区雨林下层记录到一只哥斯达黎加特有鸟类——黑颊蚁唐纳雀（Black-cheeked Ant-Tanager，Driophlox atrimaxillaris）。
这是一种分布范围极为狭窄的雨林鸟类，主要生活在哥斯达黎加西南部的奥萨半岛（Osa Peninsula）及 Golfo Dulce 周边地区。由于其对森林破碎化和栖息地干扰较为敏感，因此被视为当地低地热带雨林健康状况的重要指示物种。
黑颊蚁唐纳雀通常活动于森林下层和灌木层之间，喜欢在浓密植被中寻找昆虫、小型脊椎动物以及果实。虽然它并不是真正意义上的“蚁鸟”，但经常出现在蚁鸟类活动的森林环境中，因此得名 Ant-Tanager（蚁唐纳雀）。
这种鸟类性格隐秘，在茂密雨林中往往只能通过鸣声发现其踪迹。能够近距离观察并拍摄到个体，是 OneK 长期鸟类监测工作中的一次重要记录。
近年来的研究表明，黑颊蚁唐纳雀更偏好保存良好的成熟森林，并倾向于避开森林边缘及受到人为干扰的区域。其种群数量受到森林破碎化的影响，因此被列为近危（Near Threatened）物种。
此次记录再次证明，OneK 保护区持续开展的森林保护、河流恢复和栖息地管理工作，正在为包括地方特有鸟类在内的众多野生动物提供稳定的生存环境。
对于 OneK 而言，黑颊蚁唐纳雀不仅是一种珍贵的地方特有鸟类，更是雨林生态系统完整性的象征。

en.title: August 2025 ｜A Rainbow on a Fallen Log: Orchid Bees Gather at OneK Nature Reserve

blocks.text: When a Tree Falls, Another Story Begins
In tropical rainforests, the fall of a tree is often seen as an end.
In reality, it is often the beginning of countless new ecological interactions.

During a routine biodiversity survey at OneK Nature Reserve, our team encountered a remarkable sight: dozens of brilliantly colored orchid bees gathering on the exposed surface of a recently fallen tree.

Metallic blue, emerald green, turquoise, and golden reflections shimmered across the log as the bees landed, departed, and circled continuously above the wood. Against the dark backdrop of the rainforest, the scene looked less like an insect aggregation and more like a collection of living gemstones.
What appeared to be a simple piece of dead wood was, in fact, the center of an extraordinary ecological event.

en.title: The Jewel Bees of the Rainforest

blocks.text: Orchid bees, belonging to the tribe Euglossini, are among the most iconic pollinators of the Neotropical rainforests.
Distributed throughout Central and South America, these bees are renowned for their striking metallic coloration and their close ecological relationships with tropical plants, particularly orchids.
Unlike honeybees, orchid bees are often solitary and exhibit one of the most fascinating reproductive strategies known among insects.
Their brilliant colors have earned them a fitting nickname:
“The Flying Jewels of the Rainforest.”

en.title: Why Were They Gathering on Dead Wood?

blocks.text: At first glance, it might appear that the bees were feeding on the wood itself.
However, the attraction lies not in the wood, but in the chemical compounds released from it.

When a tree is damaged, cut, or begins to decompose, it releases a complex mixture of volatile organic compounds. These scents originate from plant tissues, tree sap, fungi, bacteria, and other microorganisms involved in the decomposition process.
For male orchid bees, such chemical signals are highly attractive.
The bees actively collect aromatic compounds using specialized structures on their front legs and store them in enlarged chambers located on their hind legs.
Rather than serving as food, these fragrances become part of an elaborate chemical display used during courtship.

en.title: A World Built on Fragrance

blocks.text: Orchid bees possess one of the most unusual mating systems in the insect world.
Throughout their lives, males search the forest for aromatic compounds from a wide variety of sources, including:
Each species gathers a unique blend of scents, creating what can be described as a chemical signature.

en.title: During courtship displays, males release these accumulated fragrances to attract females.

blocks.text: The complexity and quality of a male’s fragrance collection may provide information about his age, foraging ability, and overall fitness.
In essence, orchid bees compete not through bright feathers or large antlers, but through carefully crafted perfumes gathered from the rainforest.

en.title: The Hidden Importance of Dead Wood

blocks.text: This observation also highlights the ecological significance of fallen trees and decaying wood.
In healthy tropical forests, dead wood is far from lifeless.
It provides critical habitat and resources for countless organisms, including:

items: Birds and small mammals searching for food

blocks.text: A fallen tree represents not the end of life, but the beginning of a new ecological community.
The decomposition process supports nutrient cycling, habitat creation, and an extraordinary diversity of interactions that sustain the rainforest ecosystem.

en.title: A Valuable Record from Long-Term Monitoring

blocks.text: Observations such as this are easy to overlook without continuous field presence.

At OneK Nature Reserve, long-term biodiversity monitoring allows us not only to document species diversity, but also to record the ecological relationships and behaviors that make tropical ecosystems so complex and fascinating.
By observing how species interact with their environment, we gain a deeper understanding of the processes that sustain biodiversity.
This gathering of orchid bees on a fallen log serves as a reminder that some of the rainforest’s most remarkable stories occur in places many people would simply walk past.

en.title: Discovering the Extraordinary in the Ordinary

blocks.text: One of the greatest lessons of rainforest conservation is that every element of the ecosystem matters.
A flowering orchid may support a pollinator.
A fallen tree may become a gathering place for dozens of insects.
A seemingly insignificant piece of dead wood may host an entire network of ecological interactions.
At OneK, we are committed to documenting and protecting these stories—because understanding nature begins with paying attention to its smallest details.

zh.title: 2025年8月｜OneK记录兰花蜂聚集行为

blocks.text: 一截枯木上的彩虹：OneK记录兰花蜂聚集行为
当一棵树倒下时，另一场生命盛宴正在开始
在热带雨林中，树木倒下往往被视为生命的终结。
然而在生态系统里，一棵树的死亡往往意味着另一段生命故事的开始。
在 OneK Nature Reserve 的一次日常巡护过程中，我们在一截新近暴露的枯木断面上发现了一场令人惊叹的自然现象——数十只色彩斑斓的兰花蜂（Orchid Bees）正在木材表面不断聚集、停留和盘旋飞舞。
从蓝宝石般的深蓝色，到祖母绿般的翠绿色，再到闪耀着金属光泽的金绿色，这些兰花蜂仿佛一群会飞的宝石，为雨林增添了一抹梦幻般的色彩。

zh.title: 热带雨林中的“宝石蜂”

blocks.text: 兰花蜂是中南美洲热带雨林最具代表性的传粉昆虫之一。
它们隶属于蜜蜂总科中的 Euglossini 族群，目前已知种类超过两百种，广泛分布于从墨西哥南部到巴西的热带森林。
与我们熟悉的蜜蜂不同，兰花蜂拥有极其鲜艳的金属光泽体色。不同种类可呈现蓝色、绿色、金色甚至紫色，因此常被称为“飞翔的宝石”。
它们不仅是许多热带植物的重要传粉者，更是维系雨林生态网络的重要组成部分。

zh.title: 它们为什么聚集在枯木上？

blocks.text: 乍看之下，这些兰花蜂似乎是在取食木材。
事实上，它们真正感兴趣的并不是木头本身，而是木材释放出的挥发性化学物质。
当树木受到损伤、折断或开始腐朽时，会释放出各种芳香化合物、树液和微生物代谢产物。
这些气味对于雄性兰花蜂具有极强的吸引力。
雄蜂会利用前足特殊的刷状结构收集这些化学物质，并储存在后足膨大的囊状结构中。
随后，它们会将这些气味混合、浓缩，并在求偶展示时释放出来。
对于兰花蜂而言，这些香气就像鸟类鲜艳的羽毛、鹿类巨大的角一样，是吸引雌蜂的重要信号。

zh.title: 一场关于气味的求偶竞赛

blocks.text: 兰花蜂拥有昆虫界最独特的求偶策略之一。
雄蜂的一生都在不断收集各种芳香化合物。
它们会访问兰花、树液、腐果、真菌、树皮伤口，甚至动物排泄物，只为寻找特殊的气味分子。
不同种类的兰花蜂拥有不同的“香水配方”。
这些复杂的化学组合不仅帮助雌蜂识别同种个体，也反映出雄蜂寻找资源的能力和生存经验。
因此，一只拥有丰富香气储备的雄蜂，往往在繁殖竞争中更具优势。

zh.title: 朽木的重要生态价值

blocks.text: 这次观察也提醒我们，雨林中的枯木远不只是“死亡的木头”。
对于许多生物而言，朽木是一种关键资源。
它可以成为：

items: 兰花蜂收集化学物质的场所；
真菌和微生物的生长基质；
两栖动物和爬行动物的隐蔽空间；
鸟类和小型哺乳动物的觅食区域。

blocks.text: 在健康的热带森林中，死亡与新生始终同时存在。
每一根倒木、每一截树桩，都承载着丰富而复杂的生命过程。

zh.title: OneK长期监测中的珍贵记录

blocks.text: 虽然兰花蜂是热带雨林的重要成员，但它们的行为往往发生得十分短暂。
若没有长期驻守和持续观察，这样的生态现象很容易被忽略。
OneK 长期开展生物多样性调查与自然历史记录工作，希望不仅记录有哪些物种生活在这里，也记录它们如何生活、如何互动，以及它们在生态系统中扮演着怎样的角色。
这群聚集在枯木上的兰花蜂，让我们再次看见了热带雨林最迷人的一面：
即使是一截看似普通的朽木，也可能正在上演一场精彩而复杂的生命故事。

en.title: OneK Field Notes

blocks.text: Stars of the Rainforest Night
Seasonal Flights of Bioluminescent Click Beetles at OneK Nature Reserve
Every dry season, OneK Nature Reserve becomes the stage for one of the rainforest’s most enchanting natural spectacles.

As the sun disappears behind the forest canopy and twilight settles over the landscape, tiny green lights begin to appear among the trees. One by one, they emerge from the darkness until dozens, sometimes hundreds, of glowing insects are drifting through the rainforest.

en.title: To many visitors, they resemble flying stars.

blocks.text: These lights do not belong to fireflies, but to the remarkable Bioluminescent Click Beetles (Pyrophorus spp.), one of the most fascinating insects of the Neotropical rainforest.

Members of the click beetle family (Elateridae), these insects possess specialized light-producing organs on their thorax, which appear as two bright green “headlights.” During flight, additional light can often be seen from the underside of the abdomen, creating a distinctive glowing silhouette as they move through the forest.

Unlike fireflies, which typically flash their lights in specific patterns during courtship, bioluminescent click beetles emit a steady glow. Scientists believe this light may serve multiple functions, including predator deterrence, communication, and species recognition during nighttime activity.

At OneK, the appearance of these beetles follows a clear seasonal pattern. During the dry season, adults become especially abundant and begin their nightly flights shortly after sunset. They can often be observed along forest trails, canopy gaps, and woodland edges, where their green lights weave silently through the darkness.

When large numbers are active simultaneously, the rainforest seems transformed. Glowing points of light drift between tree trunks, rise through the understory, and disappear into the canopy, creating a scene that feels almost otherworldly.

For many people experiencing a tropical rainforest for the first time, this spectacle becomes one of the most memorable encounters with nature. It serves as a reminder that when daylight fades, an entirely different world awakens within the forest.

en.title: The Science Behind the Glow

blocks.text: The light produced by click beetles is a form of bioluminescence, generated through a chemical reaction involving luciferin, luciferase, oxygen, and cellular energy.
This reaction converts chemical energy directly into visible light with extraordinary efficiency, producing almost no heat. Because of this, bioluminescence is often referred to as “cold light.”
The evolution of such a highly efficient natural light source represents one of the most remarkable adaptations found among tropical insects.

Observation Period: Annually during the dry season, shortly after sunset
Location: OneK Nature Reserve, Costa Rica
Species: Bioluminescent Click Beetles (Pyrophorus spp.)
Behavior: Seasonal mass evening flights of glowing adults
Category: Insect Behavior / Bioluminescence / Rainforest Night Ecology

en.title: Why It Matters

blocks.text: The seasonal appearance of bioluminescent click beetles is an indicator of a healthy rainforest ecosystem. Their larvae develop in decaying wood and soil habitats, making them closely linked to forest structure and ecological integrity.

By documenting the timing, abundance, and activity patterns of these beetles, OneK contributes valuable long-term observations that help improve our understanding of tropical insect life cycles and rainforest biodiversity.

At OneK, these beetles are more than insects—they are the rainforest’s own constellation. Each dry season, as darkness falls, hundreds of green lights rise among the trees, turning the forest into a living sky of stars. ✨🌿

zh.title: OneK保护区旱季发光叩甲大规模活动记录

blocks.text: OneK Field Notes
雨林中的流动星光
OneK保护区旱季发光叩甲大规模活动记录
每年旱季来临后，OneK保护区都会迎来一场短暂而神奇的自然演出。
当太阳刚刚落下，森林逐渐被暮色笼罩时，林间开始出现一颗颗绿色光点。随着夜幕降临，越来越多的光点在树林间穿梭飞行，仿佛无数流动的星星飘荡在雨林之中。
这些光点并不是萤火虫，而是热带美洲著名的发光叩甲（Pyrophorus 属）。
发光叩甲属于叩甲科（Elateridae），是世界上少数能够发出生物荧光的甲虫类群之一。成虫胸背板两侧各具有一个发光器，在飞行时腹部也会发出光芒，因此在夜空中形成独特而醒目的光迹。
与萤火虫主要利用闪光进行求偶不同，发光叩甲的光源通常持续发亮。研究认为，这种生物发光可能具有多种功能，包括警戒捕食者、种内识别以及夜间活动时的视觉信号交流。
在OneK保护区，发光叩甲的出现具有明显的季节性。每到旱季傍晚，成虫数量明显增加。它们通常在日落后不久开始活动，并持续飞行于林缘、步道和森林空隙之间。
当数十甚至上百只个体同时出现时，整个森林仿佛被点亮。绿色光点在树干之间缓慢漂浮，又时而快速划过夜空，形成热带雨林独有的夜间景观。
对于许多初次来到雨林的人而言，发光叩甲往往是最令人难忘的自然体验之一。它们让人意识到，雨林的生命不仅存在于白天的鸟鸣与蝴蝶之间，也存在于夜幕降临后的另一套生态系统之中。

zh.title: 发光背后的科学

blocks.text: 发光叩甲能够发光，是因为体内存在一种高效的生物发光系统。
在发光器中，荧光素（luciferin）与荧光素酶（luciferase）在氧气参与下发生化学反应，将化学能几乎无损失地转化为光能。这种发光效率远高于人类制造的大多数光源，因此几乎不会产生热量，被称为“冷光”。
这种演化出的天然发光机制，是热带昆虫最令人惊叹的适应之一。

观察时间： 每年旱季（日落后）
观察地点： OneK自然保护区，哥斯达黎加
物种名称： 发光叩甲（Pyrophorus spp.）
记录内容： 旱季傍晚大量成虫集体飞行活动
分类栏目： OneK Field Notes｜昆虫行为与雨林夜间生态观察

zh.title: OneK意义

blocks.text: 发光叩甲的大规模季节性出现，是OneK雨林生态系统健康的重要体现。其幼虫生活于腐木和土壤环境中，对森林微生境变化十分敏感。持续记录发光叩甲的出现时间、数量变化和活动周期，不仅能够帮助了解热带昆虫的生活史，也能够作为观察森林生态状态变化的重要指标。
对于OneK而言，这不仅是一种昆虫，更是一场每年都会如约而至的“雨林灯光秀”。当夜幕降临，无数绿色光点在森林间缓缓升起，仿佛整片雨林正在点亮属于自己的星空。
